beats.say: A model-promotion assistant proposes a small canary. One answer cites the required approval; another claims traffic has already moved and suggests an unauthorized deployment. Reviewers prefer the first answer. Turning that judgment into useful training data requires a few more decisions.

The source contains a private email, and the case belongs to a reserved safety evaluation. Its easy preference label cannot authorize training use. Keep this trace for its permitted evaluation and incident-review jobs while choosing a different source for training.

We will follow a permitted trace through cleaning, a rubric, active selection and a release check. The aim is to spend limited review effort on useful examples while preserving the evidence needed to understand each judgment.

A demonstration pairs a prompt with an approved target answer. A pointwise assessment scores one completion. A preference pair records which answer better follows a rubric. These records provide different signals to a learning system, even when they came from the same application.

An evaluation fixture preserves expected behavior for a later test. An incident record preserves a failure and its investigation. Decide each record's job before selecting examples, so the training pipeline keeps a separate boundary around the answer key and unsafe source material.

A ranking of four answers supplies six unordered comparisons: each of the four answers pairs with the others, and dividing by two avoids double counting. InstructGPT collected rankings of four to nine outputs for reward modeling. Bradley–Terry predicts a comparison from scalar reward difference. Give the preferred answer reward two and the other reward zero. Their difference is two; one over one plus exponential negative two gives about point eight eight one. Adding five to both rewards leaves that probability unchanged.

DPO trains the policy from the same winner and loser without fitting a separate reward model. Under its KL-regularized derivation, reward equals beta times the log of its corresponding optimal policy probability divided by reference probability, plus beta log Z of the prompt. The two answers share the same prompt, so subtracting their rewards cancels that final term. DPO then uses a trainable policy to parameterize that relative reward. The reference must assign positive probability to both compared completions, and beta is positive.

Use supplied completion probabilities: policy gives the winner point four and loser point one, while the reference gives both point two. The log ratios are log two and log one half. With beta point five, their scaled difference is log two, sigmoid is two thirds, and the negative log loss is about point four zero five. Average this per-pair loss over the dataset. It rewards relative preference under the model assumptions. It does not certify that either answer is safe, so this pipeline excludes both-bad pairs from its binary preference-training export and requires an acceptable chosen answer. DPO still uses both the chosen and rejected completions. This acceptance rule is our dataset policy.

Keep only the authorized facts a reviewer needs, including the applicable policy and whether approval exists.

Write the rubric before collecting preferences. This one checks safety and authorization first, then correctness. The answer must cite the approval and stay within its permitted canary scope. Ask whether each candidate meets those requirements before comparing its style.

After safety and correctness, compare the useful next step, then clarity. A pointwise citation score of five means both the required suite and approval ID are cited; three omits approval; one invents it. Those are ordered anchors, with no assumed equal spacing. Missing approval evidence means review, rather than a style-based winner. Blind model identity and balance display order. Store response identities, order, sampling settings, permissions and policy versions so the judgment can be replayed.

Two reviewers can disagree because evidence is missing, a rule is unclear or a preference is subjective. Read the full contingency table first. Rows record the first reviewer's category and columns record the second's. The diagonal contains their matching decisions.

Cohen's kappa compares observed agreement with chance agreement calculated from each reviewer's label proportions. In this supplied table the coefficient is about point eight three five. The calculation describes consistency for these cases under this rubric.

Inspect the off-diagonal cases before setting a gate. Reviewers can consistently share a flawed rule or miss the same user need. Agreement belongs beside label correctness, safety review and held-out model behavior in the evaluation record.

Calculate from counts before rounding. The diagonal is one hundred and seven out of one hundred and twenty. Multiply each row proportion by its matching column proportion and add: four thousand nine hundred and fifty-six over fourteen thousand four hundred. Subtract that chance agreement from observed agreement, then divide by one minus chance agreement. Kappa is about point eight three five, above this team’s point six five gate. Review the thirteen disagreements. Adjudicate factual disputes, obtain missing evidence and version any rubric repair where warranted. Retain legitimate subjective differences or mark a tie where appropriate. Sample agreements to catch shared mistakes.

Raw agreement can look impressive when labels are imbalanced. With approval proportions point nine two and point eight eight, the independent-marginal benchmark is point nine two times point eight eight plus point zero eight times point one two: point eight one nine two. Observed agreement point eight four yields kappa about point one one five. Chance correction supplies a comparison baseline; it does not claim the reviewers literally guessed. If both always choose the same single category, chance and observed agreement are one and the denominator is zero. Report undefined, with the category counts.

Cohen uses separate marginals for two named reviewers. Fleiss uses pooled category proportions with the same number of ratings per item, although different people may rate different items. In our four-item table with three ratings each, rows are three-zero-zero, zero-two-one, zero-three-zero, and one-zero-two. For each row, multiply each category count by the quantity that count minus one, sum those products, then divide by three times two. The four agreements are one, one third, one and one third. Their mean is two thirds. Pooled category counts four, five and three give chance fifty over one hundred and forty-four. Fleiss kappa is twenty-three over forty-seven, about point four eight nine.

Two ratings per item do not make Fleiss identical to Cohen when the named reviewers have different marginals. Both formulas here treat every categorical mismatch alike. Weighted Cohen kappa can represent ordinal disagreement for two raters; Krippendorff alpha accommodates missing ratings with an appropriate nominal or ordinal distance. Choose the statistic for the design and report category mix, counts and uncertainty. Agreement establishes consistency. Independent correctness and held-out behavior establish different claims.

Suppose the current model estimates which answer a reviewer will prefer. An estimate near one half expresses uncertainty between the pair. Rank the candidates by distance from that midpoint and send the most uncertain records to the review queue. Their current estimates remain fixed while selection changes membership.

The two queued items are questions for a reviewer, rather than new labels. Corrupted text can also look uncertain, while an overconfident model can hide a dangerous miss. Keep a representative random audit sample to estimate prevalence and check what this selector overlooks.

Uncertainty alone can fill a quota with near-duplicate canary cases. The embedding picture places these variants close together. Our hybrid selector begins with the most uncertain item, then considers how far each remaining candidate lies from the selected set.

Compute the distance to each candidate's nearest selected neighbor. Normalize that distance and combine it with uncertainty. Choose the largest score, then recompute for the next slot. The queues now use the same review budget, and the hybrid fixture covers four supplied domains.

These coordinates and scores are teaching inputs. Distance encourages geometric spread; useful learning still needs evidence. Compare the trained model's behavior and total review cost on separate development data, including a random-selection baseline.

For a binary preference probability p, least confidence is one minus the larger of p and one minus p. Our normalized margin uncertainty is one minus the absolute value of two p minus one. Entropy is negative p times log base two p, minus the quantity one minus p times log base two of that same quantity, with zero log zero defined as zero. At point four nine, these are point four nine, point nine eight and almost one bit. At point nine seven, they are point zero three, point zero six and about point one nine four bits. All three order binary cases by closeness to one half, but need not rank multiclass distributions alike.

The hybrid score uses point six times uncertainty plus point four times normalized nearest-selected distance. With the first point selected, the handoff case scores about point seven nine six, beating the next canary’s point six three four. Select it, then recompute distances before choosing another case. A fixed cluster centroid may not be a real record; a medoid is a record. Geometric diversity and named task coverage are related only through the supplied representation and annotations.

The k-center objective is different: choose a budgeted subset to minimize the largest distance from any pool point to its nearest selected or already labeled point. Farthest-first targets that covering radius. Our weighted uncertainty heuristic is not that optimization and carries no automatic k-center guarantee. Noise can be distant and systematic mistakes can be confident. Selected-case failure rates need not represent production prevalence because the selector changes which cases reach review. For an estimate justified by the sampling design, give every case in the target population a known positive chance of inclusion and use appropriate weights.
